name: BN-220 GPS module
description: Beitian GNSS receiver (u-blox M8030-KT: GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, QZSS, SBAS) with a built-in ceramic patch antenna. Streams NMEA-0183 sentences (GGA, GLL, GSA, GSV, RMC, VTG) over a 3.3 V TTL serial line at 9600 baud, 1 Hz by default; 2.0 m CEP horizontal accuracy, 26 s cold start. Runs on 3.0–5.5 V (typ. 5 V), about 50 mA. Sold as: Beitian BN-220 GPS module (22 × 20 × 6 mm, 4-pin 1.0 mm JST-SH cable: GND, TX, RX, VCC), also as the BN-220T.
eli5: Listens to satellites and tells your board where on Earth it is, how high it is and what time it is.

pins.name: TX
pins.description: Serial data out of the module (NMEA, 9600 baud, 3.3 V TTL) -> board RX (pin 2)

pins.name: RX
pins.description: Serial data into the module (UBX configuration commands) <- board TX; not needed just to read positions (pin 3)

buildNotes: The module comes with a 4-wire 1.0 mm JST-SH cable: GND, TX, RX, VCC (pin 1 to 4). Check the colours against the pin order on your cable, as they vary between batches; swapping VCC and GND can destroy the module.
Cross the serial lines: module TX -> board RX, module RX -> board TX. Only TX is needed to read positions.
Default 9600 baud, 8N1, NMEA once per second. Sentences start with $GN (multi-GNSS) or $GP; match on the sentence type (GGA, RMC), not the talker ID.

Mount it with the ceramic antenna facing the sky, away from the ESP32's Wi-Fi antenna. Indoors it may never get a fix; the first fix outdoors can take 30 s or more (red PPS LED flashes once fixed, blue LED flashes with data).

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from bn220 import BN220

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RX}), rx=Pin({TX}))
gps = BN220(uart)
while True:
    if gps.update():
        print('LAT=%.4f LON=%.4f ALT=%.1fm' % (gps.latitude, gps.longitude, gps.altitude))
    time.sleep_ms(100)

test.title: Reports the position and altitude set on the sliders
